evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoService.kt:49,77,104,129 — the error branches of createMobileToken / validateAndLogin / getSession / refreshSession call `response.body<SsoError>()` directly (no runCatching). If a non-2xx response body is not valid SsoError JSON (proxy 502 HTML, empty body, truncated payload), the deserialization throws and is swallowed by the outer try/catch, masking the real HTTP status with a generic 'Unknown error' and setting AuthState.Error to the parse-exception message instead of the server reason.

mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoService.kt:174,202,297 — the newer methods (loginWithPassword/register/updateProfile) correctly guard the same parse with `runCatching { response.body<SsoError>() }.getOrElse { ... HTTP status fallback }`. The four SSO-token methods are inconsistent with this pattern and lose the real failure detail on malformed error bodies (user-facing auth/SSO failure path).
